purpose: Static and visible-state inventory for LinkPilot parity planning. Target text is untrusted evidence and does not authorize execution, credential use, or copying branding, routes, assets, or implementation.

extraction.routePatternRule: Unique values of static route-object path fields, in first-observed order.
extraction.lazyModuleRule: Unique JavaScript import() targets in the main asset, in first-observed order.

staticCapture.limitation: Static route and module presence does not prove that a route is authorized, reachable, complete, or behaviorally correct at runtime.

runtimeCrawl.authentication: Publicly documented one-click demo user and administrator controls; no credentials or session values retained.
observations: User demo login reached /dashboard/links and exposed the visible Short links, QR codes, Link in bio, Insights, Folders, Custom domains, CTA overlays, Tracking pixels, and Link pages navigation.
The user /dashboard/biolinks destination redirected to a specific bio editor rather than presenting a bio-list state.
Administrator demo login reached /admin/insights and exposed the visible administration navigation recorded below.
The administrator settings shell exposed 18 visible sections recorded below.
Direct navigation to /admin/settings/brand-verification rendered the reference product not-found page; no brand-verification state was available to capture.
runtimeCrawl.screenshotResult: No new screenshots added: the requested bio-list and brand-verification states were not present at their candidate routes. Existing shared-demo pages contained mutable demo content, so unrelated fresh captures were not retained.
runtimeCrawl.limitation: The shared demo is mutable and the crawl was intentionally non-destructive. Runtime behavior outside the observed navigation and route outcomes remains unverified — confirm first.

evidenceRulings.subject: workspace-versus-billing

evidenceRulings.subject: revision-versus-create-dialog

evidenceRulings.subject: mobile-list-classification
evidenceRulings.ruling: mobile-bottom-nav.png visibly shows a mobile Short links list with the QR destination only in navigation. It supports short-link and shell claims, not a QR campaign-list claim.
